plain_english_summary: The normal workflow succeeded three times on the small median task, so we now have a stable baseline. We still need matching phase-memory runs before comparing the methods.

concepts.plain_english: A result counts only when separate checks accept it.
Repeating the same comparison reduces the chance that one lucky or unlucky run controls the conclusion.
The teaching process observes verified work without controlling it.

approach.selected: Use a fresh proposal-only learning companion with bounded milestone evidence.
approach.rationale: A separate fresh agent can focus on teaching while the engineering agent keeps a small task context, and proposal-only output preserves the verification boundary.
alternatives: Teach inside the main engineering agent context.
Generate lessons only from Git history after the work.

supported: The canonical-rereading workflow is stable on the low-pressure median task.
The campaign can pause and resume without repeating completed cells.
not_supported: Bounded phase memory improves verified completion.
The current result generalizes to larger tasks.

exercise: Calculate the mean cost and time of the three completed control cells, then explain why the means cannot yet be compared with phase memory.
review_questions: Why is an agent's completion claim not sufficient evidence?
What does repeating seeds protect the experiment from?
Why can a proposal-only companion teach without changing engineering truth?

failed_experiment_lessons.lesson: A more sophisticated plan is not automatically better; keep it experimental when it adds cost without improving completion.
Monitoring signals need real labels before they can safely become advice.

exercises: Compare paired control and treatment metrics once both exist
